description: Manage wholesale products, customers, pricing, and orders.

authentication.description: Connect using a B2B Wave API key and store URL.

credentials.description: Root URL of your B2B Wave store, for example https://yourstore.b2bwave.com.

setupGuide.title: Connect B2B Wave
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need the root URL of your B2B Wave store and an active API key with access to the resources you want to use.

steps.title: Find your store URL
steps.description: Use the root URL of your B2B Wave store. If you only have a sign-in URL like https://yourstore.b2bwave.com/users/sign_in, remove /users/sign_in and use https://yourstore.b2bwave.com instead.

steps.title: Sign in to your B2B Wave admin
Open the API Keys page
steps.description: In your admin, go to Settings > API Keys.

steps.title: Create or copy an API key
steps.description: Create an API key if needed, keep it Active, and give it the scopes your integration needs. The docs list scopes such as All, Order list, Order edit, Product list, Product edit, Customer list, and Customer edit.

steps.title: Enter the connection values in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste your API key into the API Key field and enter your store root URL in the Store URL field.

name: BambooHR
description: Manage employee records, time off, benefits, and directory data

authentication.name: OAuth2
authentication.description: Connect BambooHR with OAuth2 for the MindCloud tenant using the Linear-approved BambooHR scope set, excluding stale company:info because BambooHR does not expose it as a valid OAuth scope.
authentication.scopes: openid offline_access email employee time_off employee:name employee:job payroll benefit

setupGuide.title: Connect BambooHR
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a BambooHR developer app for the MindCloud BambooHR tenant.

steps.title: Open your BambooHR developer app
steps.description: Sign in to the BambooHR Developer Portal and open the OAuth2 app you want to use for MindCloud.

steps.title: Confirm the redirect URI
steps.description: In the app settings, make sure the redirect URI is set to https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/bambooHRV2/callback.

steps.title: Grant the required scopes
steps.description: Enable the BambooHR scopes: employee, time_off, employee:name, employee:job, payroll, benefit, offline_access, email, and openid. Do not include company:info; BambooHR does not expose it as a valid OAuth scope.

steps.title: Finish the connection in MindCloud
steps.description: Return to MindCloud and start the BambooHR OAuth2 connection. Re-authenticate after scope changes so the credential picks up the updated consent.

authentication.name: Basic
authentication.description: Use BambooHR API key authentication for BambooHR endpoints that do not support OAuth2. Enter the BambooHR API key; MindCloud will send it as the Basic username and auto-fill the placeholder password.

setupGuide.title: Create a BambooHR API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the BambooHR account settings for the tenant connected to this app.

steps.title: Open Account > API Keys in BambooHR
steps.description: Sign in to BambooHR, open the account settings area, and go to Account > API Keys.

steps.title: Add a new API key
steps.description: Click Add New Key, give the key a recognizable name, and choose the permission level that matches the BambooHR data you want MindCloud to access.

steps.title: Copy the API key
steps.description: Copy the new API key and keep it somewhere secure until you finish the MindCloud connection.

steps.title: Complete the MindCloud connection
steps.description: Return to MindCloud, paste the copied value into the API Key field, and enter x in the Password field because BambooHR's Basic authentication examples use x as the placeholder password.

authentication.name: API Token (Basic Auth)
authentication.description: Enter your Beebole API token in Username. Password must be x.

setupGuide.title: Connect your Beebole account
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Beebole account with API calls enabled and an API token visible in the Beebole UI.

steps.title: Sign in to Beebole
steps.description: Open the Beebole sign-in page and log in to the account you want to connect in MindCloud.

steps.title: Enable API calls for the account
steps.description: In Beebole, open Settings > Account > Enable/Disable API calls and confirm that API access is enabled for your account.

steps.title: Reveal the API token if it is not already visible
steps.description: Open Customize > Modules, clear the settings filter, search for token, and add the API Token module so the token is shown in the Beebole UI.

steps.title: Enter the credentials in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the Beebole API token into the Username field in MindCloud. Enter x in the Password field.

steps.title: Test the connection
steps.description: Save the connection and run the Beebole test action. The recommended test action is List Companies, which should return at least your current corporate company.

authentication.name: API Key Primary
authentication.description: Primary Beehiiv API key authentication using Bearer token.

setupGuide.title: Create a beehiiv API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You must be an Owner or Admin in beehiiv to access API keys, and beehiiv requires account verification through Stripe Identity Verification before API access can be enabled.

steps.title: Open the API settings in beehiiv
steps.description: In your beehiiv account, open Settings, then select API under Workspace Settings.

steps.title: Create the API key
steps.description: Click Create New API Key. If beehiiv asks you to verify your identity, complete that verification flow first.

steps.title: Name the key and save it securely
steps.description: Enter a name for the new API key, create it, then copy the key immediately and store it somewhere secure. beehiiv only shows the full key once.

steps.title: Paste the key into MindCloud
steps.description: Return to the MindCloud beehiiv connection form and paste the copied API key into the API key field.

setupGuide.title: Connect Bexio
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Bexio account, access to the Bexio developer portal, and a Bexio app that allows MindCloud's redirect URL.

steps.title: Open the Bexio developer portal
steps.description: Sign in to the Bexio developer portal and open the app you want to connect to MindCloud.

steps.title: Verify the redirect URL
steps.description: Make sure your app has the MindCloud callback URL registered as an allowed redirect URL: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/bexio/callback.

steps.title: Copy the client credentials
steps.description: Copy the client ID and client secret from the Bexio app details page and keep them available in MindCloud.

steps.title: Start the MindCloud connection
steps.description: In MindCloud, create or edit the Bexio connection and click Connect. Sign in to Bexio and approve the requested scopes.

setupGuide.title: Connect Bigin by Zoho CRM
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to a Zoho API Console client for Bigin.

steps.title: Open your Zoho API Console client
steps.description: Sign in to the Zoho API Console and open your Server-based application for Bigin. If you do not have one yet, create a new Server-based application and choose Bigin by Zoho CRM as the service.

steps.title: Set the MindCloud redirect URI
steps.description: Add this redirect URI to the client's Authorized Redirect URIs list: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/biginByZohoCRM/callback

steps.title: Enter your Zoho client credentials in MindCloud
steps.description: Paste the Client ID and Client Secret from the Zoho API Console into the Bigin by Zoho CRM connection form.

steps.title: Sign in with Zoho
steps.description: Click Authenticate in MindCloud. Zoho will redirect you to the correct accounts server during the OAuth flow, and MindCloud will use the returned accounts-server value for token exchange.

setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Birdie user account in the workspace whose recordings or SCIM users you want to access.

steps.title: Sign in to your Birdie workspace

steps.title: Create a personal API token

steps.title: Paste the API key into the MindCloud connection

name: Bitbucket
description: Bitbucket Cloud is Atlassian's Git repository hosting and collaboration platform for repositories, pull requests, pipelines, projects, snippets, and workspace administration.

authentication.name: Bitbucket API Token (Basic)
authentication.description: Use the Atlassian account email as the username and the Bitbucket/Atlassian API token as the password for Bitbucket Cloud REST APIs.
authentication.notes: Use the Atlassian account email as the Basic auth username and the API token as the Basic auth password. Atlassian API tokens are created from the Atlassian account security page, and Bitbucket Cloud REST requests authenticate with that email-token pair.

setupGuide.title: Set up your Bitbucket API token connection
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need the Atlassian account email that owns the Bitbucket workspace plus a valid Atlassian API token with Bitbucket Cloud scopes.

steps.title: Open the Atlassian API token page
steps.description: In your Atlassian account, open the API token management page and confirm the token is active.

steps.title: Identify the Atlassian account email
steps.description: Use the exact Atlassian account email tied to the token. MindCloud stores this email as the Basic-auth username.

steps.title: Paste the email and token into MindCloud
steps.description: Enter the Atlassian account email as the username and the API token as the password for the Bitbucket connection.

steps.title: Test the workspace connection
steps.description: Use the Bitbucket Get Workspace action to verify the credential against workspace mindcloudbitbucket20260409.

name: Bluesky
description: Read Bluesky profiles, feeds, notifications, social graph data, and account session details through the official atproto HTTP API.

authentication.name: Session Token
authentication.description: Use a Bluesky app-password session and the resolved PDS URL for authenticated Bluesky and atproto requests.
authentication.notes: Bluesky's current atproto OAuth profile requires client metadata, PAR, and DPoP. This draft instead uses the documented app-password session flow and stores the exact runtime values required for authenticated requests.

credentials.name: Access Token
credentials.description: Paste the accessJwt returned by com.atproto.server.createSession.

credentials.name: Refresh Token
credentials.description: Paste the refreshJwt returned by com.atproto.server.createSession.

credentials.name: PDS URL
credentials.description: Paste didDoc.service[0].serviceEndpoint from the createSession response, including https://.

credentials.name: DID
credentials.description: Paste the did value returned by com.atproto.server.createSession.

setupGuide.title: Create a Bluesky app-password session
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Bluesky account handle and an app password created for the account you want MindCloud to use.

steps.title: Create or confirm a Bluesky app password
steps.description: Use an app password from the Bluesky account you want this connection to act as. If you need a new one, create it in the official Bluesky account settings before continuing.

steps.title: Create a session with the official createSession endpoint
steps.description: Send a POST request to Bluesky's createSession endpoint with JSON body fields identifier and password. Use your account handle as identifier and your app password as password.

steps.title: Copy the access token
steps.description: Paste response.accessJwt into the Access Token field.

steps.title: Copy the refresh token
steps.description: Paste response.refreshJwt into the Refresh Token field.

steps.title: Copy the DID
steps.description: Paste response.did into the DID field.

steps.title: Copy the PDS URL
steps.description: From response.didDoc.service, find the entry whose type is AtprotoPersonalDataServer and paste its serviceEndpoint into the PDS URL field.

steps.title: Save the connection and run the session test
steps.description: After all four fields are filled, save the connection. MindCloud will use the saved access token against the saved PDS URL for authenticated Bluesky API calls.

name: Bokun
description: Bokun signed REST API integration using Bokun access key and secret key authentication for official REST endpoints.

authentication.name: OAuth2
authentication.description: OAuth2 authorization code flow for Bokun custom or public apps.
authentication.notes: Bokun OAuth requires a Partner Dashboard app, a whitelisted MindCloud callback URL, and the vendor domain slug used to build authorize and token URLs. Bokun's public docs do not document refresh tokens for this flow.

credentials.name: Vendor Domain
credentials.description: Enter the Bokun vendor domain slug used in Bokun OAuth and API URLs, for example mytours.

credentials.name: API Key
credentials.description: Bokun calls the OAuth client ID the API key.

credentials.name: API Secret
credentials.description: Bokun calls the OAuth client secret the API secret.

setupGuide.title: Connect Bokun to MindCloud
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Bokun Partner account and a Bokun app that uses OAuth 2.0. Keep your Bokun app API key, API secret, and vendor domain handy before you start the connection.

steps.title: Create or open your Bokun app in Partner Dashboard
steps.description: In Bokun Partner Dashboard, go to Apps and create a new app or open the Bokun app you want to connect. Choose Custom app for a single-vendor build unless you need public distribution.

steps.title: Set the app URL and whitelist the MindCloud callback URL
steps.description: Add your app URL, then add this exact redirect URL to Bokun's whitelist: https://api.mindcloud.co/v1/oauth/bokun/callback

steps.title: Copy the Bokun API key and API secret
steps.description: Bokun's OAuth docs refer to the API key as client_id and the API secret as client_secret. Copy both values from the app overview page.

steps.title: Install the app for the target vendor
steps.description: For a custom app, link the app to the target vendor and complete Bokun's install flow so the vendor can grant the requested permissions.

steps.title: Enter the vendor domain in MindCloud
steps.description: When MindCloud asks for Vendor Domain, enter the Bokun vendor domain slug only, for example mytours. MindCloud uses that value to build the Bokun authorize and access-token URLs.

authentication.name: API Key (Signed REST)
authentication.description: Bokun Booking API authentication using access key, secret key, and request signing headers.

credentials.name: Access Key
credentials.description: The Bokun access key from the API key pair.

credentials.name: Secret Key
credentials.description: The Bokun secret key used to sign Booking API requests.

setupGuide.title: Connect Bokun Booking API to MindCloud
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Bokun booking channel and a Bokun API key pair for the Booking API. Bokun's REST API uses an access key, a secret key, and a request signature header on every request.

steps.title: Create or confirm a booking channel
steps.description: Bokun's Booking API works in the context of a booking channel. Make sure the vendor has the correct booking channel and currency settings before using the API key.

steps.title: Create a Bokun API key pair
steps.description: In Bokun, go to Settings, then Connections, then API keys. Create an API key with the permissions needed for the API actions you want to run.

steps.title: Enter the Bokun access key and secret key in MindCloud
steps.description: Use the Bokun access key as Access Key and the Bokun secret key as Secret Key when creating the MindCloud connection.

steps.title: Use the correct Bokun API environment
steps.description: Bokun explicitly documents the test Booking API endpoint as https://api.bokuntest.com. If you are using a test account, make sure your requests target the test environment.

name: Boomlify
description: Boomlify provides temporary email inboxes and API access for creating disposable email addresses, reading messages, managing dashboard inboxes, and checking account usage.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Boomlify API key authentication. The official docs send the credential in the X-API-Key request header.
authentication.notes: Boomlify API requests require the API key in the `X-API-Key` header. The platform API-key credential is referenced as `{{credentials.apiKey}}`; do not paste the raw key into app configuration.

steps.title: Paste the API key

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate Booqable requests with a personal access token.

setupGuide.title: Connect Booqable with an API key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need access to the Booqable account and permission to create authentication methods.

steps.title: Open User settings
steps.description: In Booqable, open User settings from the lower-left corner of the app.

steps.title: Create an API key
steps.description: Select Authentication methods, click New authentication method, choose API key, and create a key for MindCloud.

steps.title: Copy the generated key
steps.description: Copy the API key when it is shown and keep it secure. Booqable notes that API keys grant full account access.

steps.title: Use the key in MindCloud
steps.description: Enter your Booqable account URL, for example https://your-company.booqable.com, and paste the API key when configuring the MindCloud connection.

name: Boost
description: Boost.space centralizes company data, CRM, business operations, documents, tasks, and automation resources behind a workspace-specific REST API.

authentication.name: API token
authentication.description: Authenticate with a Boost.space API token. The system key is the workspace subdomain from the Boost.space URL.

credentials.name: System key
credentials.description: The Boost.space workspace subdomain before .boost.space, for example test-system from test-system.boost.space.

setupGuide.title: Connect Boost.space
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Boost.space API token with the needed permissions and the system key from your Boost.space workspace URL.

steps.title: Find your system key
steps.description: Open your Boost.space workspace and copy the subdomain before .boost.space. For example, if your workspace URL is test-system.boost.space, enter test-system in the System key field.

steps.title: Create an API token
steps.description: In Boost.space, open the main desktop, go to your profile, then API tokens. Create a token with the permissions needed for the actions you plan to use. Boost.space says token permissions cannot be edited later, so choose all needed permissions before creating it.

steps.title: Fill out the connection form
steps.description: Paste the API token into the API key field and the workspace subdomain into the System key field.

authentication.name: API Key
authentication.description: Authenticate BotHunter API requests with the access token from BotHunter settings. The token must be supplied as the shared api_key query parameter on every API method.

setupGuide.title: Set up BotHunter API key

steps.title: Open BotHunter settings

steps.title: Show and copy the token
steps.description: Click Show token and copy the access token from the field. If the token was lost or exposed, generate a new one before using it.

steps.title: Paste the token into this connection
steps.description: Paste the token as the API key credential for this app connection.

name: Botsonic
description: Botsonic is Writesonic's AI chatbot platform for generating bot responses and managing chatbot knowledge, conversations, FAQs, starter questions, and bots through REST APIs.

authentication.name: Bot REST API Token
authentication.description: Botsonic bot REST API token used for generation endpoints. Business-management endpoints require a separate USER-API-KEY credential and are intentionally blocked until that credential is available.

setupGuide.title: Connect Botsonic
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Botsonic bot REST API token. Business-management endpoints require a separate User API Key from the API Dashboard.

steps.title: Open the Botsonic bot REST API settings
steps.description: In Botsonic, open the bot you want to connect, then use the Share or REST API area documented by Botsonic to view the bot API token.

steps.title: Copy the API token
steps.description: Copy the bot REST API token. It is sent as the token header for /v1/botsonic/generate and as X-BOT-KEY for /v1/business/botsonic.

steps.title: Paste the token into the connection
steps.description: Paste the token into the API key field when creating the MindCloud connection.

authentication.name: Botsonic API Keys
authentication.description: Botsonic requires two documented API-key credentials: a bot REST API token for generation endpoints and a separate user API key for business-management endpoints.

credentials.name: Bot API Token
credentials.description: Botsonic bot REST API token used as token or X-BOT-KEY for generation endpoints.

credentials.name: User API Key
credentials.description: Botsonic User API Key used as USER-API-KEY for business-management endpoints.

setupGuide.title: Connect Botsonic API Keys
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need both Botsonic API-key credentials when using the full wrapper: the bot REST API token for generation endpoints and the User API Key for business-management endpoints.

steps.title: Copy the bot REST API token
steps.description: In Botsonic, open the bot you want to connect and use the Share or REST API area documented by Botsonic to copy the bot API token. This value is sent as token or X-BOT-KEY depending on the endpoint.

steps.title: Copy the User API Key
steps.description: Open the Botsonic or Writesonic user menu, go to API Dashboard, then Tokens, and copy the User API Key. This value is sent as USER-API-KEY for business-management endpoints.

steps.title: Paste both values into the connection
steps.description: Paste the bot REST API token into Bot API Token and the User API Key into User API Key.

name: Breakdance
description: Capture Breakdance form submissions and trigger downstream workflows

authentication.name: No Authentication
authentication.description: Breakdance sends form submissions to MindCloud through its built-in Webhook action.
authentication.notes: No Breakdance API key or OAuth setup is required for this app. Users connect Breakdance by pasting a MindCloud webhook URL into a Breakdance Form Builder webhook action.

setupGuide.title: Connect Breakdance form webhooks
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Create a MindCloud workflow with the Breakdance trigger step so you can copy its webhook URL.

steps.title: Copy the MindCloud webhook URL
steps.description: In your MindCloud workflow, add the Breakdance `On Form Submission` trigger and copy the generated webhook URL for that step.

steps.title: Open your Breakdance form settings
steps.description: In the Breakdance builder, select the Form Builder element for the form you want to connect.

steps.title: Enable the Webhook action
steps.description: In the Properties Panel, expand Actions, choose `Webhook` in `Actions After Submission`, and open the Webhook settings.

steps.title: Paste the MindCloud webhook URL and map fields
steps.description: Paste the MindCloud webhook URL into `Webhook URL`. Use `Field Map` to send the form fields you want MindCloud to receive. Add headers only if your workflow explicitly requires them.

steps.title: Submit a live test from the front end
steps.description: Refresh the form on the front end and submit a test entry so MindCloud receives a real Breakdance payload.

setupGuide.title: Connect your Bridge application
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: You need a Bridge sandbox or production application. Bridge says sandbox credentials are only for testing and should not be used in production.

steps.title: Sign in to Bridge Dashboard
steps.description: Open the Bridge dashboard and sign in to the application owner account for the environment you want to connect.

steps.title: Create or open your Bridge application
steps.description: Bridge documents that after you create a sandbox application on the dashboard, Bridge provides a client_id and client_secret for that application.

steps.title: Copy the client ID and client secret
steps.description: Copy the client_id and client_secret shown for the application. Keep the client_secret private so only your server-side systems can use it.

steps.title: Use Bridge user access tokens only when an action asks for one
steps.description: For authenticated aggregation actions, first run the Authorization token action to mint a short-lived Bridge user access token, then paste that token into the action input that asks for it.

steps.description: In the Browse AI dashboard, open an approved robot that this wrapper should run or inspect.

steps.title: Open the Integrate tab and copy the robot details
steps.description: On the robot page, click Integrate. In the "Integrate using Rest API" section, copy the Robot ID and Workspace ID, and review the robot input parameters shown there.

steps.title: Create the MindCloud test connection
steps.description: In MindCloud, open the Browse AI app connection form and paste your API key into the API Key field. Leave robot-specific values for the test action or action arguments when prompted.

setupGuide.title: Connect Bumpups API Key
setupGuide.beforeYouBegin: Sign in to your Bumpups account. You only need one API key for this connection.

steps.title: Open the API settings page
steps.description: In Bumpups, go to Settings > API.

steps.title: Enable API access
steps.description: Click Enable API if API access is not already enabled for the account.

steps.title: Create a new API key
steps.description: Click + Create API Key, optionally enter a name, and create the key.

steps.title: Choose permissions
steps.description: Select All to allow every documented endpoint, or Restricted if you only want specific endpoints.

steps.title: Copy the API key
steps.description: Copy the new key and paste it into the MindCloud connection form.

authentication.name: AccessKey Header
authentication.description: Use your bunny.net account API key as the Bunny Core API AccessKey header. This app does not use bearer authorization.
authentication.notes: Stores one secret field named apiKey and injects it only as the AccessKey header for requests to api.bunny.net.
